#!/bin/zsh
# [KPMG] 2026
: <<'SCRIPT_INFO' ============================================================================= Teams Chat Deep Link - Extension Attribute ============================================================================= Description: Reports a Microsoft Teams deep-link URL that opens a 1:1 chat with the currently logged-in console user. Sources the user's email address from whichever identity mechanism is actually populated on the Mac:
1. Jamf Connect - UserEmail key within the console user's com.jamf.connect.state.plist 2. Platform SSO (PSSO) - the registered IdP account (typically a UPN/email) embedded within the console user's dsAttrTypeStandard:AltSecurityIdentities attribute
Returns "Not Available" if no console user is logged in, or if neither source yields a usable email address.
Author: Russell Collis Created: 29/07/2026 Updated: 29/07/2026 Version: 3.0
Notes: v1.0 sourced email via dscl EMailAddress (found unpopulated in this environment). v2.0 switched to Jamf Connect's com.jamf.connect.state.plist (UserEmail key), which works where Jamf Connect performs an interactive login. v3.0 adds a Platform SSO fallback for Macs where Platform SSO handles authentication instead of (or alongside) Jamf Connect, and where the state plist may not exist or may not be populated as a result.
Requirements: EITHER: - Jamf Connect installed with at least one successful login completed by the console user, OR - Platform SSO configured and the console user registered against it (AltSecurityIdentities populated)
Output: String - Microsoft Teams deep-link URL, or "Not Available"
IMPORTANT: This script is specifically designed for KPMG's macOS environment and should only be deployed within KPMG's managed infrastructure. It contains organisation-specific configurations and should not be used outside of this intended environment. ============================================================================= ============================================================================= Changelog ============================================================================= 29/07/2026 - v1.0 - Russell Collis - Initial version, converted from standalone snippet into a Jamf Pro Extension Attribute with console user detection, email validation, and a proper <result> output block. Sourced email via dscl EMailAddress (later found to be unpopulated for this environment). 29/07/2026 - v2.0 - Russell Collis - Reworked email lookup to read UserEmail from Jamf Connect's com.jamf.connect.state.plist instead of the dscl EMailAddress attribute, per confirmed working lookup method. 29/07/2026 - v3.0 - Russell Collis - Added a Platform SSO fallback: where the Jamf Connect state plist doesn't exist or isn't populated, the script now attempts to parse the registered IdP account (email/UPN) out of the console user's dsAttrTypeStandard:AltSecurityIdentities attribute instead, so the EA works correctly on Macs authenticating via Platform SSO. ============================================================================= SCRIPT_INFO
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------- # Determine the currently logged-in console user (ignoring root and # loginwindow, which stat -f%Su can occasionally return during odd # session states, e.g. at the login window with nobody signed in). # ----------------------------------------------------------------------- consoleUser=$(stat -f%Su /dev/console)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------- # Guard clause: bail out early with a safe EA result if there's no genuine # interactive console user currently logged in. # ----------------------------------------------------------------------- if [[ -z "$consoleUser" || "$consoleUser" == "root" || "$consoleUser" == "loginwindow" ]]; then echo "<result>Not Available</result>" exit 0 fi
assignedUserEmail=""
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------- # SOURCE 1: Jamf Connect # Build the path to the console user's Jamf Connect state plist, where # Jamf Connect stores the authenticated user's email address (UserEmail) # following a successful interactive login. # ----------------------------------------------------------------------- jamfConnectStateLocation="/Users/${consoleUser}/Library/Preferences/com.jamf.connect.state.plist"
if [[ -f "$jamfConnectStateLocation" ]]; then assignedUserEmail=$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print :UserEmail" "$jamfConnectStateLocation" 2>/dev/null) fi
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------- # SOURCE 2: Platform SSO (fallback) # Only attempted if Source 1 didn't yield anything. Platform SSO writes # its registration details into dsAttrTypeStandard:AltSecurityIdentities # on the local user record, with the registered IdP account (typically a # UPN/email address) embedded in that string after "PlatformSSO:". # # Splitting on the literal string "SSO:" isolates the value that follows # "PlatformSSO:" (the "Platform" portion is split off, leaving the # account identifier), which is then trimmed of any leading whitespace. # ----------------------------------------------------------------------- if [[ -z "$assignedUserEmail" ]]; then pssoAccountIdentifier=$(dscl . -read "/Users/${consoleUser}" dsAttrTypeStandard:AltSecurityIdentities 2>/dev/null \ | awk -F'SSO:' '/PlatformSSO/ {print $2}' \ | sed -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//')
# Only accept the parsed value if it actually looks like an email # address (contains an '@'), to avoid building a malformed deep link # from an unexpected AltSecurityIdentities format. if [[ "$pssoAccountIdentifier" == *"@"* ]]; then assignedUserEmail="$pssoAccountIdentifier" fi fi
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------- # Build and return the Teams deep-link URL if either source above # yielded a usable email address; otherwise report gracefully. # ----------------------------------------------------------------------- if [[ -n "$assignedUserEmail" ]]; then teamsDeepLink="https://teams.microsoft.com/l/chat/0/0?users=${assignedUserEmail}" echo "<result>${teamsDeepLink}</result>" else echo "<result>Not Available</result>" fi
exit 0
